Not to me. To the idiot claiming that a theory is "logical Philosophy and has limited scientific basis."

You see something. Then you say, I think this thing I saw is this. You design a test to exercise your theory about what that thing you saw might actually be. You conduct the test and observe the results - to see if your idea can be verified. Based upon this work, you draw a conclusion about that thing you saw. Either it is this, or it is not this, but something else. The initial observation should be observable by others, and the test conducted should be duplicable by others. If your theory is correct, they should be able to duplicate your experiment.

Success in all of these areas still does not mean your theory is correct. The results observed can be caused for entirely different reasons.
